arxiv-2007-14870.title: Decoding machine learning benchmarks
arxiv-2007-14870.creator: Lucas F. F. Cardoso, Vitor C. A. Santos, Regiane S. Kawasaki Francês, Ricardo B. C. Prudêncio, Ronnie C. O. Alves
arxiv-2007-14870.description: Abstract Despite the availability of benchmark machine learning (ML) repositories (e.g., UCI, OpenML), there is no standard evaluation strategy yet capable of pointing out which is the best set of datasets to serve as gold standard to test different ML algorithms.

arxiv-2201-02709.title: Detecting Anomaly in Chemical Sensors via L1-Kernel based Principal Component Analysis
arxiv-2201-02709.creator: \IEEEauthorblockN Hongyi Pan \IEEEauthorrefmark 1, Diaa Badawi \IEEEauthorrefmark 1, Ishaan Bassi \IEEEauthorrefmark 2, Sule Ozev \IEEEauthorrefmark 2, Ahmet Enis Cetin \IEEEauthorrefmark 1 \IEEEauthorieeemembermark 1 \IEEEauthorblockA \IEEEauthorrefmark 1Department of Electrical and Computer Engine
arxiv-2201-02709.description: Abstract We propose a kernel-PCA based method to detect anomaly in chemical sensors. We use temporal signals produced by chemical sensors to form vectors to perform the Principal Component Analysis (PCA). We estimate the kernel-covariance matrix of the sensor data and compute the eigenvector corresponding to the largest eigenvalue of the covariance matrix.

arxiv-2205-05447.title: Notes on Spinors and Polyforms II: Quaternions and Octonions
arxiv-2205-05447.creator: Niren Bhoja, Kirill Krasnov
arxiv-2205-05447.description: Abstract Pauli matrices are 2 × 2 2\times 2 tracefree matrices with a real diagonal and complex (complex-conjugate) off-diagonal entries. They generate the Clifford algebra Cl ⁡ ( 3 ) {\rm Cl}(3) . They can be generalised by replacing the off-diagonal complex number by one taking values in either quaternions or octonions (or their split versions).

arxiv-2210-16867.title: Geometrical effects on the downstream conductance in quantum-Hall–superconductor hybrid systems
arxiv-2210-16867.creator: A. David, J. S. Meyer, M. Houzet
arxiv-2210-16867.description: Abstract We consider a quantum Hall (QH) region in contact with a superconductor (SC), i.e., a QH-SC junction. Due to successive Andreev reflections, the QH-SC interface hosts hybridized electron and hole edge states called chiral Andreev edge states (CAES). We theoretically study the transport properties of these CAES by using a microscopic, tight-binding model.

arxiv-2304-07359.title: CHEMICAL COMPOSITIONS OF RED GIANT STARS IN THE OLD OPEN CLUSTER NGC 7789 linemake (https://github.com/vmplacco/linemake), MOOG (Sneden 1973), IRAF (Tody 1986, Tody 1993), SPECTRE (Fitzpatrick & Sneden 1987)
arxiv-2304-07359.creator: Neel Nagarajan, Christopher Sneden, Melike Afşar, Catherine A. Pilachowski
arxiv-2304-07359.description: Abstract We have gathered optical-region spectra, derived model atmosphere parameters, and computed elemental abundances for 15 red giant stars in the open cluster NGC 7789. We focus on the light element group CNOLi that provides clues to evolutionary changes associated with internal fusion events and chemical mixing.

arxiv-2310-10990.title: A second-order exponential integration constraint energy minimizing generalized multiscale method for parabolic problems
arxiv-2310-10990.creator: Leonardo A. Poveda, Juan Galvis, Eric T. Chung
arxiv-2310-10990.description: Abstract This paper investigates an efficient exponential integrator generalized multiscale finite element method for solving a class of time-evolving partial differential equations in bounded domains. The proposed method first performs the spatial discretization of the model problem using constraint energy minimizing generalized multiscale finite element method (CEM-GMsFEM). This approach consists of two stages.

arxiv-2508-12126.title: Strong Field Scattering of Two Black Holes: Exploring Gauge Flexiblity
arxiv-2508-12126.creator: Adam Clark, Geraint Pratten
arxiv-2508-12126.description: Abstract Recent advances in post-Minkowskian (PM) gravity provide new avenues for the high precision modelling of compact binaries. In conjunction with the Effective One Body (EOB) formalism, highly accurate PM informed models of binary black holes on scattering trajectories have emerged.

arxiv-2512-13928.title: Codifference as a measure of dispersion and dependence for mixture models
arxiv-2512-13928.creator: Jakub Ślęzak
arxiv-2512-13928.description: Abstract Codifference is a commonly used measure of dependence for stable vectors and processes for which covariance is infinite. However, we argue that it can also be used for other heavy-tail distributions and it provides useful information for other non-Gaussian distributions as well, no matter the tails.

arxiv-2601-18269.title: The Most Luminous H β \beta Reverberation Mapping of E1821+643 Indicates the Lower Boundary of the Radius-Luminosity Relation PyRAF ( Science Software Branch at STScI 2012 ) , DASpec ( Du 2024 ) , PyCALI ( Li 2024 ) , JAVELIN ( Zu et al. 2011 ) .
arxiv-2601-18269.creator: Sha-Sha Li, Hai-Cheng Feng, Jiancheng Wu, J. M. Bai, H. T. Liu, Kai-Xing Lu, Mouyuan Sun, Jian-Guo Wang
arxiv-2601-18269.description: Abstract The radius-luminosity ( R BLR R_{\rm BLR} - L 5100 L_{5100} ) relation is fundamental to active galactic nucleus (AGN) studies, enabling supermassive black hole (SMBH) mass estimates and AGN-based cosmology applications. However, its high-luminosity end remains poorly calibrated due to insufficient reliable reverberation mapping (RM) data.

pmc-10606304.title: Recent and Advanced DNA-Based Technologies for the Authentication of Probiotic, Protected Designation of Origin (PDO) and Protected Geographical Indication (PGI) Fermented Foods and Beverages
pmc-10606304.creator: Vincenzina Fusco, Francesca Fanelli, Daniele Chieffi
pmc-10606304.description: The authenticity of probiotic products and fermented foods and beverages that have the status of protected designation of origin (PDO) or geographical indication (PGI) can be assessed via numerous methods. DNA-based technologies have emerged in recent decades as valuable tools to achieve food authentication, and advanced DNA-based methods and platforms are being developed.

pmc-10774661.title: Ventricular fibrillation and ventricular tachycardia post–SARS-CoV-2–targeted mRNA/viral vector vaccination
pmc-10774661.creator: Ashish Kumar, Mariam Shariff, Justin Lee, Siddarth Agarwal, Zain Asad, Daniel C DeSimone, Abhishek Deshmukh, Christopher V DeSimone
pmc-10774661.description: messenger RNA (mRNA)/viral vector vaccination from the beginning of the vaccination until May 2023. In the U.S. a total of 516 ventricular fibrillation/ventricular tachycardia (VF/VT) (167 VF and 349 VT) events were reported as an adverse event post severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2)–targeted messenger RNA (mRNA)/viral vector vaccination from the beginning of the vaccination until May 2023.

pmc-11339379.title: The effect of novel vitamin D3 compounds on saliva samples from COVID-19 patients: a lab study
pmc-11339379.creator: Sarah M. Nizar Feteih, Ashraf Dada, Emily L. G. Heaphy, Samar Zailaie, Dania Jan, Zinab Rashed, Ghassan Wali
pmc-11339379.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Vitamin D has shown antimicrobial effects. This study aimed to explore the antiviral effects of vitamin D3 on saliva samples collected from patients with coronavirus disease-19 (COVID-19) and compare saliva and swab results to aid in policy development. Saliva and swab samples were collected from adult patients with a positive test for COVID-19 at the King Faisal Specialist Hospital and Research Centre, Jeddah. Patients who were immunocompromised and pregnant and aged < 18 years were excluded.

pmc-11536291.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). pmc-11657659.title: Transcriptomic and proteomic sequencing unveils the role of vitamin D and metabolic flux shifts in the induction of human hepatic organoids
pmc-11657659.creator: Shule Zhang, Linghong Liu, Xianyu Li, Tiancheng Zhou, Qing Shi, Dong Li, Xiuli Ju
pmc-11657659.description: BackgroundHepatic organoids (HOs), validated through comparative sequencing with human liver tissues, are reliable models for liver research. Comprehensive transcriptomic and proteomic sequencing of HOs throughout their induction period will enhance the platform’s utility, aiding in the elucidation of liver development’s molecular mechanisms.

pmc-11692421.title: THE PSYCHOSOCIAL EFFECTS OF EXPRESSIVE ARTS THERAPY ON PATIENTS WITH AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION
pmc-11692421.creator: Rainbow Tin Hung Ho, Temmy L T Lo, Wai Chi Chan, Allen M Y Cheong, Qing Li, Adrian H Y Wan
pmc-11692421.description: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is the leading cause of central vision loss in older adults. With irreversible vision loss, patients with AMD also experience psychosocial distress, which is given less attention. This study aims to evaluate the psychosocial effects of Expressive arts therapy (EXAT) on patients with AMD.

pmc-11714064.title: Sildenafil is a candidate drug for Alzheimer’s disease: Real‐world patient data observation and functional validation in patient iPSC‐derived neurons and the 5xFAD mouse model
pmc-11714064.creator: Yichen Li, Dhruv Gohel, Pengyue Zhang, Andrew A Pieper, Jeffrey L Cummings, Feixiong Cheng
pmc-11714064.description: BackgroundOur previous study identified that Sildenafil (a phosphodiesterase type 5 [PDE5] inhibitor) is a candidate repurposable drug for Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) using in silico network medicine approach. However, the clinically meaningful size and mechanism‐of‐actions of sildenafil in potential prevention and treatment of AD remind unknown.

pmc-12721328.title: DNA extrusion size determines pathway choice during CAG repeat expansion
pmc-12721328.creator: Mayuri Bhatia, Ashutosh S Phadte, Anna Lakhina, Anthony R Monte Carlo III, Sarah Barndt, Anna Pluciennik
pmc-12721328.description: DNA triplet repeat expansion causes several primarly neurological disorders like Huntington’s disease, myotonic dystrophy type 1, and fragile-X related disorders. There is general consensus that recognition of extrahelical extrusions or hairpin-loop structures (formed by strand slippage) by the DNA mismatch repair protein MutSβ leads to repeat expansion by a mutagenic process.

pmc-13247209.title: Inboard advance of arc magmatism regulates mountain building in the Andes
pmc-13247209.creator: Tomas N Capaldi, Brian K Horton, Chelsea Mackaman-Lofland, Facundo Fuentes, Gustavo Ortiz
pmc-13247209.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Debate continues over the mechanisms that govern the tempo and style of arc magmatism and retroarc deformation along ocean-continent plate boundaries. Here we integrate detrital and bedrock geo/thermochronological and geochemical records of Cenozoic arc magmatism with results on the spatiotemporal evolution of retroarc shortening and flexural subsidence to explore the interactions and feedbacks among subduction, magmatism, and crustal deformation in the southern Central Andes.

pmc-13261977.title: An exploratory investigation of β-aminoisobutyric acid as a biomarker: possible relationships between urinary BAIBA and lifestyle habits
pmc-13261977.creator: Miu Suzuki, Yuki Shimba, Ayana Sakai, Aika Kobayashi, Sayuri Shibayama, Chika Takahashi, Moe Shibata, Tae Kiyosawa, Yuichiro Obana, Yuhi Yamada, Toshio Hosaka
pmc-13261977.description: Backgroundβ-Aminoisobutyric acid (BAIBA) is a metabolite of valine and thymine and has been identified as a myokine released from skeletal muscle in response to exercise. Experimental studies have suggested that BAIBA exerts multiple metabolic effects, including promotion of adipose tissue browning and improvement of glucose metabolism.

pmc-13609104.title: From Rapid Progression to Long-Lasting Complete Response: A Wide Range of Ripretinib Activity for Metastatic GIST—A Real-World Cohort
pmc-13609104.creator: Hanna T. Frumin Edri, Walid Shalata, Ilia Berezhnov, Tanzila Tairov, Tatiana Bobrovitsky, Dan Mirelman, Esther Tahover, Ofer Purim, Yuval Dadon, Katerina Shulman, Gali Perl, Gil Bar Sela, Maria Passhak, Ronen Brenner
pmc-13609104.description: Background: Ripretinib, a switch-control kinase inhibitor approved for advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumor (GIST), inhibits primary and secondary KIT and PDGFRA mutations. Real-world data from Western and Middle Eastern populations remain limited. We report outcomes from a molecularly characterized Israeli multicenter cohort. Methods: We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study across seven university-affiliated medical centers in Israel.

pmc-13643955.title: Construction of a predictive nomogram for ICU mortality in patients with cardiac arrest using the MIMIC-IV database and the eICU Collaborative Research Database
pmc-13643955.creator: Wei Shi, Xuemei Hu, Hui Li, Qihui Huang, Dian Zhou, Min Yang
pmc-13643955.description: BackgroundCardiac arrest (CA) is a critical clinical event associated with extremely high mortality and long-term disability. This study aimed to identify risk factors associated with ICU mortality and develop a practical nomogram for risk prediction to support prognostic assessment and risk stratification among patients with CA.MethodsA retrospective analysis was conducted using two large public critical care databases.
